assignment: A source-isolated participant joins a legally replayed developer checkpoint. Evaluate only the assigned scene range through normal logical observations. Earlier actions were developer setup, not participant choices. Skim earned cards naturally and read optional material only when useful. Explain expected and observed contributions, concrete clarity or confusion, and any repeated work. This is bounded partial-context passage evaluation, not fresh full-campaign play or voluntary retention. Other vignettes within the same condition may have been seen; the other condition and source are withheld.

playerReport.scope: Partial-context assigned vignette: chapter 3 only. Events 1–26 are developer setup, not my play. No earlier gameplay or later chapters assessed.

intelligibility.explanation: The justice rule contributes a general prescription and the weapon request a harmful counterexample. The result makes their conflict explicit. The later bridge is understandable after reading the setup eclipse item.

learning.explanation: The sequence distinguishes finding a counterexample from finding a complete replacement definition. It then separates examined choices from prestige and makes claims answerable to objections.

construction.explanation: Repayment can do harm becomes an unsettled definition, then supports two distinct outcomes. The final card explains objections but drops the eclipse input's specific contribution of stated conditions; I inferred that bridge rather than seeing it spelled out.

pacing.explanation: Four combinations finish the scope without repeating a recipe. The second card restates the weapon failure before adding the important lack of replacement. Initial chapter card remained visible after the first combination until dismissal. Repeated read at 35 was my output-display handling error, not required game work.

continuity.explanation: Within this checkpoint, the harmed-repayment result carries into the definition and both final goals. The supplied eclipse explanation provides a cross-topic link after optional reading; I cannot assess its earlier acquisition because that was setup.

choice.explanation: There was one substantive pairing at the start and at the next step. After the unsettled definition I could choose which of two goal branches to complete first, but both were required. Partner reversal is not a distinct choice.

playerReport.experience: Logical-player account only, not evidence of human enjoyment. I predicted the dangerous exception and examined-life result. I chose the prestige branch first, then read the carried-over explanation to understand its contribution. The work did not ask me to rebuild a result. My main uncertainty was how explicitly conditions from an eclipse were being carried into a general objections principle.
playerReport.stoppingReason: Assigned chapter 3 goals complete at event 36; stopped without advancing.
playerReport.nextExperiment: Ask a fresh human player to explain why the conditions item contributes to the final combination before reading its result; observe whether the bridge is legible without the partner list doing the selection.
